A woman in her early 40’s was seen in the Inflammatory bowel diseases clinic for routine assessment.

attribution_limitations: The biochemical results are called unremarkable, yet C-reactive protein 6.9 mg/L is printed beside a normal range of below 5 mg/L; the sentence does not say which listed values the word unremarkable covers.

The abstract says the patient proceeded with a total colectomy, whereas the case description names a laparoscopic total proctocolectomy with end ileostomy; the source does not reconcile the two terms.

The endoscopic disease activity scores are tied only to the time of colonoscopy; the case text mentions a colonoscopy in 2022 and recurrent biopsy and dilation over the following 18 months without saying which examination the scores come from.

case_context.index_subject_description: Woman in her early 40s with ulcerative colitis, primary sclerosing cholangitis and a rectal stricture

evidence.quote: A woman in her early 40’s was seen in the Inflammatory bowel diseases clinic for routine assessment.
We report a middle-aged lady who developed a rectal stricture on the background of ulcerative colitis and primary sclerosing cholangitis.
A woman in her early 40’s
a middle-aged lady
A woman in her early 40’s
She was diagnosed with UC pancolitis in 1999
with large duct PSC in 2022 confirmed on magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography
ongoing progressive disease activity
She had no known history of endometriosis
had no other past medical history
She unfortunately developed steroid dependency
developing complications of steroid induced osteoporosis
evidence of a rectal stricture on endoscopy
Colonoscopy in 2022 demonstrated a rectosigmoid stricture
repeated histology did not demonstrate any evidence of dysplasia
initial endoscopic biopsies showed no dysplasia
our patient had a further increased malignancy risk due to the presence of two high-risk features including PSC and presence of an undifferentiated colonic stricture
The differential diagnosis included both malignant and benign strictures.
Given her risk factor of PSC and persistence of the rectal stricture, malignancy was highly concerning even though prior superficial biopsy samples were negative.
Benign stricture secondary to IBD was also considered.

Other causes of benign strictures including diverticulosis, ischaemia, radiation, and endometriosis were considered less likely given no history of the same and investigations to date were unremarkable for these.
